findings.description: Copy-fallback cannot self-heal: once a host falls back to `cpSync` because `symlinkSync` threw, every later `agent-init` run returns "kept (not a symlink)" for that target and never re-syncs it, even after `.agents/skills` changes.
The new `doctor` skills-reachability check crashes with an unhandled `ENOTDIR` exception on exactly the scenario its own comment says it exists to catch: a symlink materialized as a text file.

The Cursor "Skills" cell adds a `.claude/skills/` "for compatibility" clause that is unsourced and unsupported anywhere else in the PR, violating this repo's own sourcing rule for tool-capability claims.
findings.body:
**Concern:** this PR changes the Cursor Skills cell to:

```
`.agents/skills/` native, plus `.cursor/skills/`, and `.claude/skills/` for compatibility
```

The `.claude/skills/` clause is new and appears nowhere else: not in the accompanying prose (`docs/capability-matrix.md` lines 44-47, which only covers `.agents/skills/` alongside `.cursor/skills/`), not in decision 24 in `docs/design/0001-architecture.md`, not in the PR body/commits, not in `README.md`, and `src/plan.utils.ts` never emits any `.claude/skills` action for Cursor. No `## Sources` entry backs it either.

**Rule cited** (AGENTS.md, "Rules specific to this repo"):
> Never claim parity a tool does not have. A capability gap is documented in the matrix, not emulated.
> Facts about the five tools come from their docs, with the source and date recorded in the matrix.

Separately (weaker, but same root cause): even the *supported* `.agents/skills/` claim isn't reflected in the file's "Verified against" table — the Cursor row (line 124) still reads `2026-09-14 | docs only`, unbumped, even though the prose two sections above cites "read 2026-09-18" for this fact.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agent-init/blob/c4e0d8de9e3323c7635df2cc219109c729c27404/docs/capability-matrix.md#L17

findings.description: A second "three of the five tools" count for the same skills-discovery fact was left stale when this PR updated the count to "four of the five" earlier in the same file.
findings.body:
**Concern:** this PR updates a "three of the five" claim to "four of the five" at README.md lines 50-51 (Cursor now also reads `.agents/skills/` natively), but line 100 makes the identical claim about the identical fact and was not touched:

> They install once into `.agents/skills/`, where three of the five tools find them with no further wiring.

This now contradicts the paragraph the PR itself updated 50 lines above, in the same file — exactly the "updated in one file and stale everywhere else" failure this project's own README names as its reason for existing.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agent-init/blob/c4e0d8de9e3323c7635df2cc219109c729c27404/README.md#L100-L100
findings.suggestion: They install once into `.agents/skills/`, where four of the five tools find them with no further wiring.

findings.description: Decision 17's "still unbuilt" list still names the Windows symlink fallback (decision 3) as unbuilt, contradicting the new decision 24 this PR adds, which documents that same fallback as now built.
findings.body:
**Concern:** decision 17 (unchanged by this PR) reads:

> Still unbuilt and now recorded honestly: the version stamp (decisions 1 and 9), a symlink-failure fallback for Windows (decision 3), and interactive tool/pack selection (decision 10 — today the interactive path is a single confirm, and every option is reachable by flag).

This PR's new decision 24 ("## 24. Windows, and one fewer symlink") opens with "The symlink fallback decision 3 promised" and documents it as now built: the link falls back to copying, `--check` treats a faithful copy as non-drift, and `doctor` gained a per-tool check. Decision 17's claim is now false and self-contradicts decision 24 within the same document — a reader trusting decision 17's list would believe the Windows fallback still doesn't exist.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agent-init/blob/c4e0d8de9e3323c7635df2cc219109c729c27404/docs/design/0001-architecture.md#L301-L303

findings.description: The `.agents/skills/README.md` content this tool writes into every scaffolded repo still says "Claude Code and Cursor reach it through a symlink," which this PR's own Cursor change makes false.
findings.body:
**Concern:** this string, unconditionally written into every scaffolded repo as `.agents/skills/README.md`, was not updated by this PR:

```ts
content: `# Skills\n\n...\n\nCodex, opencode and Mistral Vibe read this path natively. Claude Code and Cursor reach it\nthrough a symlink.\n`,
```

This PR's own change elsewhere in the same file (the Cursor block now emits `{ kind: "skip", target: ".cursor/skills", reason: "cursor reads .agents/skills natively" }` instead of a symlink/copy-dir action) makes "Claude Code and Cursor reach it through a symlink" false — only Claude Code still symlinks. The PR correctly updated the same fact in `README.md`, `docs/capability-matrix.md`, and the new decision 24, but missed this fourth copy, which is the one that actually ships into end users' repositories.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agent-init/blob/c4e0d8de9e3323c7635df2cc219109c729c27404/src/plan.utils.ts#L231

findings.description: The bare `catch {}` around `symlinkSync` swallows every failure, not just Windows' EPERM, so a genuinely broken `action.to` or an unrelated permissions/disk error would silently present as the expected "copied (symlinks unavailable here)" fallback instead of surfacing as a bug.

The new doctor skills check calls `readdirSync(dir)` twice for the same directory (once to compute `reachable`, once more inside the ternary to build the `detail` string) — a local `count`/`entries` variable would avoid the duplicate read.

New doctor-output copy this PR adds ("resolves to nothing — the tool will load no skills") introduces an em-dash in newly-added prose, per this repo's reviewer house style against em/en dashes in new copy.

`sameTree()` only walks entries in `from`, so extra files present in `to` but absent from `from` are never flagged as drift; this PR's new symlink-fallback drift check inherits that one-directional comparison from the unmodified, pre-existing helper.

process_issues.description: review-security was not spawned: the diff touches only local filesystem scaffolding (symlink/copy fallback, a doctor check, docs) with no auth, network, secrets, or other trust-boundary surface. Noted for coverage transparency.
